# Go API reference

<!-- Generated by go/internal/docgen from Go source. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Package `github.com/nebius/contree-client/go/v1`.

Generated from the exported Go declarations and doc comments, including client methods, models, helpers, and test doubles. See the [Go client guide](api.md) for usage.

Package contree provides a generated, typed client for the Contree v1 API.

Construct a Client with NewClient, or use ResolveProfile and NewClientFromProfile for saved credentials. Pass contexts to every operation, and close byte download streams. Event and pagination methods return iter.Seq2 iterators; check their errors inside the range loop. Event streams close automatically when iteration ends.

(go-contreehome)=
### ContreeHome

ContreeHome returns the directory that contains Contree configuration files. CONTREE\_HOME has priority over XDG\_CONFIG\_HOME and ~/.config/contree.


(go-decodechunk)=

DecodeChunk decodes a typed stream payload, raw JSON, or a raw object to bytes. Unknown shapes and invalid base64 return empty bytes so a live stream can continue.


(go-loadprofiles)=
### LoadProfiles

LoadProfiles reads cli.ini and auth.ini and returns profiles and the active profile name. auth.ini values override cli.ini values. Pass no path to use the default auth.ini location, or pass one explicit auth.ini path.

```go
func LoadProfiles(path ...string) (map[string]Profile, string, error)
```

(go-newtestclient)=
### NewTestClient

NewTestClient constructs a normal Client and its offline MockTransport. It uses "test-token" and [https://contree.test](https://contree.test) by default. Options can change normal client settings; the mock HTTP transport is always installed last. No request can fall back to a network transport.

For code that constructs its own client, supply a zero-value MockTransport through WithHTTPClient instead.

```go
func NewTestClient(options ...ClientOption) (*Client, *MockTransport, error)
```

**Example**

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	contree "github.com/nebius/contree-client/go/v1"
)

func permissions(ctx context.Context, client *contree.Client) (map[string]bool, error) {
	me, err := client.WhoAmI(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("get token permissions: %w", err)
	}
	return me.Permissions, nil
}

func main() {
	client, mock, err := contree.NewTestClient()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("create test client: %v", err)
	}
	err = mock.Mock(contree.OpWhoAmI, contree.WhoAmIResponse{
		Permissions:    map[string]bool{"spawn": true},
		OperationsStat: map[string]int64{},
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("mock token permissions: %v", err)
	}
	allowed, err := permissions(context.Background(), client)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("load permissions: %v", err)
	}
	fmt.Println(allowed["spawn"])
	fmt.Println(len(mock.CallsFor("WhoAmI")))
}
```

Output:

```text
true
1
```

### type APIConnectionError

APIConnectionError reports a connection or response-read failure. TimedOut distinguishes deadline and socket timeout failures.

```go

	Method   string
	URL      string
	TimedOut bool

}
```

(go-apierror)=
### type APIError

APIError identifies normalized connection, HTTP status, and SSE errors. Use errors.As with this interface to recognize them through wrapped errors.

```go
type APIError interface {
	error
	// contains filtered or unexported methods
}
```

(go-apistatuserror)=
### type APIStatusError

APIStatusError reports an HTTP response that the operation did not accept. Body contains at most the runtime error-body limit. Details contains the decoded "error" property when present, or the decoded response otherwise. A non-nil RetryAfter preserves the header even when its value is zero.

```go
type APIStatusError struct {
	StatusCode int
	Method     string
	URL        string
	RequestID  string
	Body       []byte
	Details    any
	Traceback  []string
	RetryAfter *time.Duration
}
```

(go-apistatuserror-error)=
#### APIStatusError.Error

```go
func (e *APIStatusError) Error() string
```

(go-newclientfromprofile)=
#### NewClientFromProfile

NewClientFromProfile constructs a client from a loaded profile. Resolve and construct a saved profile as follows:

	profile, err := ResolveProfile("")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	client, err := NewClientFromProfile(profile)

ClientOption values are applied after the profile settings. Thus, caller options override the profile URL and project.

```go
func NewClientFromProfile(profile Profile, options ...ClientOption) (*Client, error)
```

(go-client-ensurefile)=
#### Client.EnsureFile

EnsureFile returns the existing file with the content digest, or uploads content when the server returns NotFoundError for that digest.

(go-client-spawninstance)=
#### Client.SpawnInstance

SpawnInstance starts an instance and returns the full response without waiting for execution to finish. Image accepts a tag:NAME reference or a bare image UUID. Pass SpawnInstanceOptions{} to use the server defaults.

The response preserves all documented fields and their absent, null, and value states. Check response.UUID before using it to wait for or follow the operation. Use SpawnInstanceWithResponse for exact JSON states in request options.

```go
func (c *Client) SpawnInstance(
	ctx context.Context,
	command string,
	image string,
	options SpawnInstanceOptions,
) (InstanceSpawnResponse, error)
```

**Example**

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	contree "github.com/nebius/contree-client/go/v1"
)

func main() {
	client, mock, err := contree.NewTestClient()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("create test client: %v", err)
	}
	if err := mock.Mock(contree.OpSpawnInstance, contree.InstanceSpawnResponse{UUID: contree.Some("operation-1")}); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("mock instance creation: %v", err)
	}
	response, err := client.SpawnInstance(
		context.Background(),
		"wc -l < /work/data.txt",
		"tag:ubuntu:latest",
		contree.SpawnInstanceOptions{
			Shell:      true,
			Env:        map[string]string{"LC_ALL": "C"},
			Cwd:        "/work",
			Timeout:    time.Minute,
			Disposable: true,
		},
	)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("spawn word-count command: %v", err)
	}
	operationID, ok := response.UUID.Value()
	if !ok || operationID == "" {
		log.Fatal("spawn response has no operation ID")
	}
	fmt.Println(operationID)
}
```

Output:

```text
operation-1
```

(go-client-waitoperation)=
#### Client.WaitOperation

WaitOperation returns the terminal response, including failed and cancelled responses unchanged. By default it reads the operation kind, follows instance events, and polls image imports every 500 milliseconds. An unknown kind uses events. Supply at most one options value to select a mode explicitly. The event stream stays open until completion, EOF, a transport error, or context cancellation, or an inactivity timeout. Ping frames keep it open. IdleTimeout defaults to 15 seconds and resets on incoming data, including ping frames. It never extends the overall context deadline. A completion event still requires a terminal status response. The context bounds the entire wait, including status reads and polling delays.

```go
func (c *Client) WaitOperation(
	ctx context.Context,
	operationID string,
	options ...WaitOperationOptions,
) (OperationResponse, error)
```

(go-mockcall)=
### type MockCall

MockCall records an HTTP attempt, including attempts made by helpers and retries. Operation is the canonical generated method name. PathParams uses the wire parameter names. Body contains the serialized request body.

```go

	Operation  string
	Method     string
	URL        string
	Path       string
	PathParams map[string]string
	Query      url.Values
	Header     http.Header
	Body       []byte
}
```

(go-mockresponse)=
### type MockResponse

MockResponse supplies a wire response for MockHTTP. BodyError, when set, is returned after all Body bytes have been read. StatusCode must be explicit.

```go
type MockResponse struct {
	StatusCode int
	Header     http.Header
	Body       []byte
	BodyError  error
}
```

(go-mocktransport)=
### type MockTransport

MockTransport is an offline HTTP transport with outcome queues and a call log. Its zero value is ready to use. Configuration, requests, and log access are safe for concurrent use. Each queue repeats its last outcome.

Mock operation names, such as SpawnInstance or ListImages. Helpers such as SpawnInstance, EnsureFile, and IterImages execute normally through those mocks. Full-response and byte-stream aliases share the operation's queue and call log.

```go
type MockTransport struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

(go-mocktransport-calls)=
#### MockTransport.Calls

Calls returns an independent snapshot of all recorded HTTP attempts.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) Calls() []MockCall
```

(go-mocktransport-callsfor)=
#### MockTransport.CallsFor

CallsFor returns a snapshot for one generated operation, in request order. Unknown names return an empty snapshot. Stream aliases use the canonical name.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) CallsFor(operation string) []MockCall
```

(go-mocktransport-mock)=
#### MockTransport.Mock

Mock queues a typed result for a generated operation. Use an Op descriptor, model values for JSON, struct{}{} for empty responses, \[]byte for byte responses, and \[]OperationEvent for SSE responses. Results are serialized now and decoded by the real client when called.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) Mock[T any](operation Operation[T], result T) error
```

(go-mocktransport-mockerror)=
#### MockTransport.MockError

MockError queues an error. APIStatusError and its typed wrappers become HTTP responses, so status handling and retries run normally. Other errors become transport failures wrapped in APIConnectionError and remain accessible through errors.Is and errors.As. Nil errors are rejected.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) MockError(operation string, err error) error
```

(go-mocktransport-mockhttp)=
#### MockTransport.MockHTTP

MockHTTP queues an exact HTTP response. Use it for malformed JSON, specific status codes or headers, and encoded bodies such as gzip. Input bytes and headers are copied, and each call receives a fresh response body.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) MockHTTP(operation string, response MockResponse) error
```

(go-mocktransport-mockstream)=
#### MockTransport.MockStream

MockStream queues byte or SSE results followed by a read error. Result uses the same representation as Mock. A nil error produces normal end-of-stream.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) MockStream[T any](operation Operation[T], result T, err error) error
```

(go-mocktransport-roundtrip)=
#### MockTransport.RoundTrip

RoundTrip records the request and returns its next configured outcome. It never opens a connection. Unconfigured requests return NotMockedError.

```go
func (m *MockTransport) RoundTrip(request *http.Request) (*http.Response, error)
```

(go-retrypolicy)=
### type RetryPolicy

RetryPolicy controls retries for idempotent buffered requests. MaxAttempts includes the initial request. One disables retries; zero retries until the context ends. The client timeout applies separately to each buffered attempt.

```go
type RetryPolicy struct {
	Statuses     []int
	ServerErrors bool
	Delays       []time.Duration
	MaxAttempts  int
	RetryUnsafe  bool
}
```

(go-spawninstanceoptions)=
### type SpawnInstanceOptions

SpawnInstanceOptions configures SpawnInstance. Zero scalar values and nil maps, slices, and pointers omit their fields so the server defaults apply. Non-nil empty maps and slices are sent as empty JSON objects and arrays.

Use SpawnInstanceWithResponseOptions with SpawnInstanceWithResponse to send explicit zero or null values for fields that SpawnInstanceOptions would omit.

```go
type SpawnInstanceOptions struct {
	Disposable  bool
	Hostname    string
	Args        []string
	Shell       bool
	Env         map[string]string
	PreserveEnv bool
	PreserveCwd bool
	Cwd         string
	UID         int64
	GID         int64

	ResourcesLimits *InstanceResourcesLimits
	// Networking defaults to enabled. Set Enabled to Some(false) to disable it.
	Networking *InstanceNetworking
	Stdin      *ClosableStreamRepr

	// Timeout limits server execution, independently of the request context.
	// Zero uses the server default. Positive durations round up to whole seconds.
	// Negative durations return an error before sending a request.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// TruncateOutputAt limits captured bytes per stream. Nil uses the server
	// default (1 MiB); a pointer to zero sends an explicit zero.
	TruncateOutputAt *int64
	Files            map[string]FileSpec
}
```

(go-spawninstancewithresponseoptions)=
### type SpawnInstanceWithResponseOptions

SpawnInstanceWithResponseOptions contains optional arguments for SpawnInstanceWithResponse.

```go
type SpawnInstanceWithResponseOptions struct {
	Disposable       Optional[bool]
	Hostname         Optional[string]
	Args             Optional[[]string]
	Shell            Optional[bool]
	Env              Optional[map[string]string]
	PreserveEnv      Optional[bool]
	PreserveCwd      Optional[bool]
	Cwd              Optional[string]
	UID              Optional[int64]
	GID              Optional[int64]
	ResourcesLimits  Optional[InstanceResourcesLimits]
	Networking       Optional[InstanceNetworking]
	Stdin            Optional[ClosableStreamRepr]
	Timeout          Optional[int64]
	TruncateOutputAt Optional[int64]
	Files            Optional[map[string]FileSpec]
}
```

(go-waitoperationoptions)=
### type WaitOperationOptions

WaitOperationOptions selects how WaitOperation observes completion.

```go
type WaitOperationOptions struct {
	// IdleTimeout is the maximum gap between incoming SSE data in seconds.
	// Nil uses 15 seconds. Zero disables the limit. Ping frames reset it.
	IdleTimeout *float64

	// FollowEvents defaults to nil: follow instance events and poll image imports.
	// True forces events; false polls status without opening an event stream.
	FollowEvents *bool
}
```
